TESTIMONY OF DENISE GARLAND, DEPUTY COMMISSIONER
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs Hearing Date: March 5, 2025 Hearing Time: 10:00 a.1n.
"An Act to Provide Support Services for Military Members
Transitioning to Civilian Life in Maine"
Good morning, Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and members of the
Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. My name is Denise
Garland, and I am the Deputy Commissioner of the Department of Economic and
Community Development or DECD for short. I am here today to testify neither for nor against LD 620 - An Act to Provide Support Services for Military Members
Transitioning to Civilian Life in Maine.
In 2021, $200,000 in one-time funds were provided to DECD from the Federal ARP funds designated in 2021 Public Laws, Chapter 483, Part II. The legislation
directed DECD, in consultation with the Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services, to
design a pilot project for outreach and support services for active-duty military
members who would be transitioning to civilian life. I thought it might be helpful
to share some of the results of that pilot project that went to Boots2Roots through a
competitive process. Boots2Roots engaged in a proactive workforce attraction marketing campaign that included military magazine advertisements, billboard placement and in-person and virtual military job fairs in and around military installations. Additionally, these funds enabled Boots2Roots to increase their resume coaching, interview coaching and transition coaching programs. At the end of the pilot program, Boots2Roots enrolled 190 military members, Veterans and
Page 1 of 2

military spouses in the Transition to Work Program. Prior to this funding, annual
enrollment was approximately 32 military members.
Other results from this pilot project showed that 94 percent of the candidates
who completed the Boots2Roots program found work within 60 days of arriving in
Maine. 80 percent of enrollees were married with children and 85 percent purchased
a home within twelve months of arriving in Maine. 65 percent of those participants
were not originally from Maine and neither was their spouse.
Every year, approximately 200,000 men and women leave U.S. Military
service and return to life as civilians. Twelve to eighteen months before they leave, these service members are actively seeking where to transition. Having a permanently funded program is key to the success of ensuring Maine is promoted as a welcome place for transitioning military members and their families.
If it is the pleasure of the Committee, DECD is willing to accept the funding
and work collaboratively with Maine Bureau of Veteran's Services to ensure funds
are provided to organizations conducting outreach and providing support services to
active-duty military members and their families who are transitioning to civilian life.
This concludes my testimony for the Department of Economic and
Community Development.

Testimony ofRep. Parnell Terry presenting
LD 620, An Act to Provide Support Services for Military Members

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs
Committee, I am Representative Parnell Terry of District 108, which includes part of Gorham. I
am here today to present LD 620, An Act to Provide Support Services for Military Members
Transitioning to Civilian Life in Maine.
In the 130th Legislature this committee and the whole legislature approved an appropriation of
$200,000 to help recruit newly retired military members from all over the country to come live and work in the state of Maine. This was a pilot program to see if this kind of work would be successful in bringing new families with solid work experience and the desire to lay roots in our
incredible state.
The pilot program was a huge success. With that small appropriation dozens of new families made the move to Maine, helping to add a $45 million return on investment to the state.
Boots2Roots is one such organization doing this incredible work. They partner with companies
and commtmity development organizations including Live and Work Maine, Dead River
Company, Bath Iron Works, Northem Light Health, Unum and many others, to connect veterans
and their families to meaningful employment, helping them integrate seamlessly into
communities across the state. They are now also partnering with a range of educational institutions like The Landing School, Maine Upward Bound and the Roux Institute to help even more retiring military members and their families find opportunities in Maine.
In 2024, Boots2Roots had record enrollment and has supported more than 825 new Mainers in
putting down roots -- significantly contributing to Maine's workforce and impacting Maine's

District 108: Gorham (part)

economy. These servicemembers and their families share the unparalleled work ethic and sense of grit that Mainers are so well known for, making this a natural fit.` During a time when so many businesses across the state are struggling to hire and retain quality employees, and our state is struggling with an aging Workforce, organizations like Boots2Roots don't just benefit the retiring service members, but they also provide a sorely needed benefit to the state by fostering connection between dedicated and hardworking individuals and businesses
experiencing workforce shortages.
Supporting these efforts is a win-win for all of us, and I am so proud to advocate for this Work. Thank you for your time. I am happy to answer any questions you may have.

Testimony in Support of:

]oint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs

Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and distinguished members of the ]oint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. I'm Steven Lanning, Deputy Director of the Maine
Bureau of Veterans' Services. I'm here today to testify neither for nor against L.D. 620, "An Act to
Provide Support Services for Military Members Transitioning to Civilian Life in Maine."
I would like to thank Deputy Commissioner Garland and the Department of Economic and Community Development (DECD) for their leadership in implementing the pilot program and for sharing its outcomes. The success of the pilot project, administered through Boots2Roots, highlights the importance of transition services for military members and their families. The ability to provide proactive outreach and support to those transitioning to civilian life strengthens Maine's workforce and communities.

Military transition can present challenges, especially for those unfamiliar with the region. Ensuring
sustained support for transition services would help address these challenges and provide military members with the resources needed for successful integration into Maine's workforce and
communities.

The Bureau supports Deputy Commissioner Garland's testimony and DECD's willingness to
accept the funding. DECD has demonstrated the ability to oversee the appropriations as set forth under LD 620. The Bureau remains committed to supporting efforts that assist service members in
their transition and stands ready to collaborate with DECD, and other stakeholders on this
important issue.

We appreciate the Committee's attention to this matter and welcome any questions you may have.

Respectfully Submitted,

Executive Summary
Boots2Roots enjoyed another strong year of growth in 2024 with Teammate enrollment and Teammate hires each reaching all-time highs. This growth is a result of the investments of employer and community partners, a talented staff, and a group of volunteers dedicated to
achieving best outcomes for veterans. Momentum is continuing into 2025 with 108 Teammates
actively looking for work in Maine and 10 hires already this year.
Boots2Roots ended 2024 in a strong financial position thanks in large part to Federal and State grant awards, a significant local nonprofit financial gift and the support of over 30 Maine business
partners. We are actively working to extend funding commitments beyond the Federal and State
grant funding windows.
Suitable housing remains the most significant challenge to our Teammates' transitions to Maine going into 2025. This was confirmed by results of a recent survey of newly transitioned
Tearnmates. We are fortunate to have a passionate group of volunteers assisting to overcome this
challenge, but we see this challenge continuing to present the greatest obstacle to more dramatic
program increases
Mission
Boots2Roots assists active-duty military members, Veterans and military spouses find meaningful work in Maine while providing a pipeline of workforce talent to Maine employers.
Boots2Roots fills an important gap as the only organization in Maine exclusively working with active-duty military members 12-18 months before they separate from service. Boots2Roots'
Transition-to-Work program helps teach servicemembers how to express their military service in ways that civilian hiring managers will understand. The program also provides important access to a network of peer mentors, Maine employers and community partners who are ready to assist
with all aspects of transition, including realtors, veterans' benefits, medical contacts, educational resources, etc. Attracting more military talent to Maine's workforce is another important element of Boots2Roots' program.
Together with the state, employers, and community partners we are working to make Maine the destination of choice for more of the 150,000 active-duty military who transition to civilian life
each year.

Goal 1: Active duty servicemembers, Veterans and spouses ("Teammates") will find meaningful
